A1.justification: Both PDFs describe REI-Bench and TOCC. Their complete main texts and appendices, including figures and tables, support comparison despite substantial expansion and reorganization in v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original AI2-THOR planning experiments, prompting comparisons, error analyses, and execution cases in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains original simulation results and adds planner comparisons, human planning outcomes, context-removal experiments, and token/latency measurements.

M1.justification: TOCC retains the same procedure: resolve references using context, rewrite the instruction explicitly, and plan from the rewrite (v1 Section 3.4; v3 Section 3.3). The revised prompt and new Algorithm 1 document this existing procedure. Gated AP and CoT variants concern comparison methods.

E1.justification: Reported ALFRED task coverage narrows from seven tasks in v1 to six in v3, which explicitly excludes Pick Two & Place and lists zero samples for it in Table 5. The household domain, AI2-THOR environment, and nine RE/context combinations remain.

E2.justification: v3 adds a DAG-Plan-style reimplementation, an adapted HPE planner, GPT-4o+SayCan, and a human reference. Prompting comparisons add ICL, while Table 6 also evaluates gated AP and short/segmented CoT variants. SayCan, LLM+P, and the six original backbones remain represented in Appendix A.

E3.justification: v3 changes the dialogue-effect reference from successfully selected seed instructions to generated explicit instructions with context removed. It adds instruction-only controls across RE levels, human evaluation on a 100-sample subset, and per-step token/latency metrics. The 1,000-task stratified subset is newly documented; this does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The new context-removal ablation tests whether dropping dialogue can reproduce TOCC's benefit, finding that it fails for implicit references. v3 also adds quantitative efficiency comparisons of prompting variants and a bread/lettuce distractor failure case in Figure 6. Original error breakdowns and appendix execution cases are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates for its experiments. The new human subset size and average latency/token measurements do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v3 adds planner and human scores, ICL and instruction-only results, and efficiency measurements. Some retained entries also change: Ministral-8B+SayCan's Noised Context/Implicit REs score is 22.4% in v1 Figure 6 and 27.4% in v3 Figure 7. Many original scores remain identical. The 100% and 57.7% dialogue-reference results use different instruction inputs and are not a same-setting performance comparison.

T1.justification: Neither version presents mathematical theorems, proofs, or derivations. v3's expanded linguistic motivation and implementation pseudocode do not introduce substantive mathematical reasoning; the three RE levels and three context types remain conceptually unchanged.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain REI-Bench, analysis of reference-related failures, and TOCC. v3 narrows the novelty claim from the first study of instruction vagueness in robot planning to the first systematic modeling grounded in pragmatics. The abstract's maximum reported success-rate drop changes from 77.9% to 36.9%.

C2.justification: v3 expands the mechanism explanation to argue that planning fails to engage otherwise available language-understanding abilities, and discusses limitations of dependency graphs and structured memory. Its conclusion adds specific boundaries concerning selected simple tasks, short horizons, absent multimodal perception, and simulator-only validation, replacing v1's brief caveat about other forms of vagueness.

D1.justification: v3 adds detailed generation/replacement prompts, OntoNotes example sourcing, filtering counts, prompting-variant descriptions, TOCC pseudocode, and project/code access information. Appendix A newly specifies the 1,000-task stratified subset and task counts. Conversely, v1's explicit statements about excluding robot replies from planner inputs and using one PDDL domain file are no longer documented.

R1.justification: v3 replaces the assertion that embodied linguistic vagueness is unexplored with discussion of clarification and uncertainty approaches. New Table 1 positions REI-Bench against AmbiK, CLARA, KNOWNO, DialFRED, and CLAQUA, supporting the narrower novelty claim. Additional linguistic and planning references substantially expand the positioning.

P1.justification: Substantial passages describing the motivation, problem framing, dataset construction, TOCC, and supplementary findings are rewritten. The separate problem-formulation subsection is absorbed into Approach, Appendix B is reorganized into four subsections, and Appendix C expands into structured method descriptions. These exceed local language corrections.

P2.justification: Figures 2 and 3 are redrawn, benchmark heatmaps are expanded and reorganized, and radar charts receive additional series, revised legends, and different main-text model selection. v3 adds comparison, task-distribution, efficiency, and filtering tables, plus a new failure figure and algorithm display. Original appendix case figures are retained with renumbering.

improvement.justification: Replacing v1's selected-seed reference with context-stripped generated instructions makes the dialogue comparison better controlled. New context ablations, broader comparisons, fuller prompts, and explicit limitations improve support and transparency. However, v3 leaves AP results inconsistent between Tables 3 and 8, introduces filtering counts in Table 9 that conflict with Section 3.1, and reports efficiency percentages inconsistent with Table 6. These issues limit the net quality gain.
